description: Fires mostly in middlegame positions (about 12-26 stones) where column 1 holds exactly one stone while column 0 is started and the center columns 2-3 are built up (7+ stones together). Any second stone in column 1 shuts it off. This is necessary-ish but far from sufficient: most such boards do not fire, and late-game boards give weak near-threshold activation. No single clean pattern was found.
effect: Small: when strongly active it lowers the probability of playing column 1 by about 4-8 points when column 1 is a live candidate; otherwise no measurable change.
program:
def fires(b):
    h = b.heights
    return h[1] == 1 and h[0] >= 1 and 12 <= b.ply <= 26 and h[2] + h[3] >= 7

def level(b):
    h = b.heights
    if h[1] > 1:
        return 1 if b.ply >= 30 else 0
    s = 1
    if h[1] == 1: s += 2
    if h[0] >= 1: s += 1
    if 12 <= b.ply <= 26: s += 2
    if h[2] + h[3] >= 7: s += 2
    return s
notes: Best dev F1 0.25 (P 0.225, R 0.281, AUROC 0.63) for col1==1 & col0>=1 & ply 12-26 & h2+h3>=7. Simulation share negative (-0.06) for every program. Column-1 height is the only robust signal: 94% of top-band firing has exactly one stone there, and adding a col1 stone kills activation in every edit test. Beyond that, edit sweeps show configuration-specific dependencies (opponent at (3,3)/(3,2), me at (0,0)) that do not generalize. Could be a polysemantic or random direction. Synthesis 1 hits 5.41 > dev max 5.355.
